chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabie, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who was appointed guardian over an orphan's wealth, so he borrowed something from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) had borrowed wealth from the orphans who were in his guardianship.'
ai.seo_question: Can a guardian borrow money from an orphan's wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of a guardian borrowing from an orphan's wealth, citing the precedent of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) as a definitive legal proof (hujjah). In Shia jurisprudence, this precedent supports the flexibility in managing orphan assets for their benefit, provided the borrowing is done with proper accountability and does not constitute misappropriation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid Bin Jareer, from Abu Al Rabie, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>

was asked about a man who governed some wealth of an orphan, so he borrowed something from it, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> had borrowed from the wealth of the orphans who were in his<sup>asws</sup> lap (care)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from abu al-Rabi‘ who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who becomes the person in charge of the assets of orphans and borrows a certain amount thereof. He (the Imam) said, ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, would borrow from the assets of orphans under his guardianship.’”
